title: Ireland's Economy Looks Strong on Paper · 24 Aug
keywords: Ireland, inflation, cost of living, fuel excise, budget 2026, consumer prices, Irish economy, EU fiscal policy, energy costs, housing costs, transport costs, purchasing power, European Central Bank
notes: Ireland's headline economic indicators remain robust, with strong tax receipts and resilient employment, yet consumers continue to face a cost-of-living squeeze that official data cannot fully capture. Inflation held at 3.4% in July 2026 for the second consecutive month, keeping purchasing power under pressure. A government decision to delay planned fuel excise increases has sharpened the political debate, raising questions about whether short-term relief can substitute for structural reform.
